title: Oatcakes with cheddar and Bramley apple

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, flour, bicarb, butter, Bramleys, brown sugar and cheddar are all plain home staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: A bowl, rolling pin, baking tray and small pan are ordinary kit, and a glass will do for cutting rounds.

works.reason: The oat dough ratio, 20 minutes at 190°C and a quick Bramley purée with cheddar give a sensible snack for four.

honest_times.reason: 18 minutes covers making and rolling the dough, peeling the apples and slicing the cheese, and the 20 minutes of baking matches the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Stewed Bramley with cheddar is a classic March store-apple pairing, and the apple is a main topping rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are plain, clear British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Wholegrain oats, cheese and fruit with little sugar make a filling, real-food snack.
